title: Unique Nutty Egyptian Lentils Pilaf
description: A flavorful and nutritious Egyptian dish featuring lentils, goose fat, and a blend of spices, perfect for a weeknight dinner. This recipe is also Buddhist-temple-friendly as it does not contain any animal by-products except for goose fat which can be substituted with a vegan alternative.
instructions: Heat the goose fat in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
Add the cumin, coriander, salt, and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Add the green lentils and 2 cups of water to the saucepan, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, or until the lentils are tender.
Fluff the lentils with a fork and stir in the chopped fresh parsley.
Serve hot, garnished with additional parsley if desired.
Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
